what: Evacuations in Guam as super typhoon Bavi approaches

clean_source_blocks.text: Rain falls in Saipan, Northern Mariana Islands, ahead of super typhoon Bavi's arrival Emergency evacuations are taking place in Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands as a super typhoon bears down on the US Pacific territories. Bavi is forecast to make landfall early on Monday morning, with winds of up to 257km/h (160mph), according to the US National Weather Service (NWS). It warned the "very dangerous" storm could cause "catastrophic" damage, with "significant flooding from torrential rains" possible and waves potentially nearly 11m (35ft) high on Monday. The western Pacific region is particularly prone to tropical cyclones - though storms of this strength are unusual for the US islands.
The storm is forecast to bring winds in excess of 160mph and waves nearly 11m high when it makes landfall on Monday.

The island's civil defence office said at 13:00 local time (03:00 GMT) on Sunday that one of the evacuation sites had already reached maximum capacity and that people were being redirected to another site. Bavi is currently hurtling towards the US Pacific territories and is due to make landfall early on Monday Bavi has been classified as a super typhoon by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), a part of the US Navy responsible for monitoring tropical storms in the western Pacific. A super typhoon has winds in excess of 130 knots (150mph). JTWC predicts that Bavi will have winds of 150 knots (173mph) when it arrives over the islands, with gusts reaching as high as 180 knots (207mph). The NWS considers super typhoons to have the equivalent destructive potential as a category four or five hurricane.

Super Typhoon Bavi rapidly intensified in the western Pacific Ocean and is forecast to strike the U.S. Mariana Islands, including Guam, as a super typhoon by Monday. Devastating winds, torrential rain and powerful storm surge are all possible. Bavi first became a tropical storm late Wednesday, and by early Friday it strengthened into a typhoon, which is what hurricanes are called in the western Pacific Ocean north of the equator. The storm reached super typhoon strength later in the day. It is centered more than 300 miles east of Guam, moving west at 7 mph. Despite being so far away, outer bands of the super typhoon are already starting to hit the U.S. Mariana Islands. As the forecast map below shows, Super Typhoon Bavi is expected to continue its west-northwest track over the next several days.

Emergency evacuations are taking place in Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands as a super typhoon bears down on the US Pacific territories.

Bavi is forecast to make landfall early on Monday morning, with winds of up to 257km/h (160mph), according to the US National Weather Service (NWS).

It warned the "very dangerous" storm could cause "catastrophic" damage, with "significant flooding from torrential rains" possible and waves potentially nearly 11m (35ft) high on Monday.

The western Pacific region is particularly prone to tropical cyclones - though storms of this strength are unusual for the US islands.

Bavi is expected to pass directly over Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands by Monday afternoon, but the NWS warned that destructive conditions could be felt eight to 10 hours from the storm's centre.

"The window is rapidly closing to evacuate if directed to do so by local officials, or if your home is vulnerable to high winds or flooding," the agency said, adding that winds "will pose a deadly threat to those venturing outside".

Guam, usually a sun-soaked tourist destination with a population of about 170,000, has opened five evacuation centres in its schools. These sites have a maximum capacity of around 1,700 and are primarily intended for vulnerable people.

The island's civil defence office said at 13:00 local time (03:00 GMT) on Sunday that one of the evacuation sites had already reached maximum capacity and that people were being redirected to another site.

The NWS considers super typhoons to have the equivalent destructive potential as a category four or five hurricane.

The National Weather Service said the Marianas will start feeling the impacts of Super Typhoon Bavi as it makes it approach to the islands.

It is expected to strengthen as it continues toward the Marianas, generally on a west-northwestward track, with a slight increase in forward speed. payload.title: Guamissa ja Pohjois-Mariaaneilla evakuointeja supertaifuuni Bavin lähestyessä
payload.summary: Supertaifuuni Bavin ennustetaan iskevän Guamiin ja Pohjois-Mariaaneille varhain maanantaina. Viranomaiset varoittavat erittäin vaarallisesta myrskystä, joka voi tuoda tuhoisia tuulia, rankkasateita, tulvia ja lähes 11-metrisiä aaltoja.
payload.content:
Supertaifuuni Bavin lähestyminen on käynnistänyt evakuointeja Guamissa ja Pohjois-Mariaaneilla, jotka ovat Yhdysvaltain alueita läntisellä Tyynellämerellä. Myrskyn ennustetaan saapuvan saarille varhain maanantaina, ja viranomaiset varoittavat sen voivan aiheuttaa erittäin vaarallisia olosuhteita, kuten tuhoisia tuulia, rankkasateita, tulvia ja voimakasta aallokkoa.

## Evakuointipaikat täyttyvät

Guamin väestönsuojeluviranomainen kertoi sunnuntaina kello 13 paikallista aikaa, että yksi evakuointipaikoista oli jo saavuttanut enimmäiskapasiteettinsa. Ihmisiä ohjattiin sen vuoksi toiseen paikkaan. Samaan aikaan Bavi eteni kohti Yhdysvaltain Tyynenmeren alueita, ja sen ulkoreunojen kerrottiin jo alkaneen vaikuttaa Yhdysvaltain Mariaaneilla.

Myrskyn keskus oli yli 300 mailia Guamasta itään ja liikkui länteen noin seitsemän mailin tuntinopeudella. Ennusteen mukaan Bavin odotetaan jatkavan länsi-luoteista reittiä seuraavien päivien aikana. Läntinen Tyynimeri on erityisen altis trooppisille hirmumyrskyille, mutta näin voimakkaat myrskyt ovat Yhdysvaltain saarilla harvinaisia.

## Tuulten ennustetaan olevan poikkeuksellisen voimakkaita

Yhdysvaltain kansallinen sääpalvelu varoitti, että Bavi voi tuoda mukanaan jopa 257 kilometrin tuntinopeuden tuulia. Sääpalvelun mukaan erittäin vaarallinen myrsky voi aiheuttaa katastrofaalisia vahinkoja, ja rankkasateiden seurauksena merkittävät tulvat ovat mahdollisia. Aaltojen ennustetaan voivan nousta maanantaina lähes 11 metriin.

Joint Typhoon Warning Center on luokitellut Bavin supertaifuuniksi. Sen mukaan supertaifuunissa tuulet ylittävät 130 solmua eli 150 mailia tunnissa. Keskuksen ennusteessa Bavin tuulten arvioidaan olevan saarille saapuessa 150 solmua eli 173 mailia tunnissa, ja puuskien voivan nousta 180 solmuun eli 207 mailiin tunnissa. Yhdysvaltain kansallinen sääpalvelu pitää supertaifuuneja tuhovoimaltaan neljännen tai viidennen kategorian hurrikaania vastaavina.

## Bavi voimistui nopeasti

Bavi voimistui nopeasti läntisellä Tyynellämerellä. Se kehittyi trooppiseksi myrskyksi myöhään keskiviikkona, vahvistui taifuuniksi varhain perjantaina ja saavutti supertaifuunin voimakkuuden myöhemmin samana päivänä. Alueella hurrikaaneja vastaavia myrskyjä kutsutaan taifuuneiksi, kun ne syntyvät päiväntasaajan pohjoispuolisella läntisellä Tyynellämerellä.
summary_bullets: Guamissa ja Pohjois-Mariaaneilla on käynnissä evakuointeja supertaifuuni Bavin lähestyessä.
Myrskyn ennustetaan tuovan tuhoisia tuulia, rankkasateita, tulvia ja lähes 11-metrisiä aaltoja.
Yksi evakuointipaikka oli sunnuntaina jo täyttynyt, ja ihmisiä ohjattiin muualle.

Alueella hurrikaaneja vastaavia myrskyjä kutsutaan taifuuneiksi, kun ne syntyvät päiväntasaajan pohjoispuolisella läntisellä Tyynellämerellä.

article.source_text:
Rain falls in Saipan, Northern Mariana Islands, ahead of super typhoon Bavi's arrival Emergency evacuations are taking place in Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands as a super typhoon bears down on the US Pacific territories. Bavi is forecast to make landfall early on Monday morning, with winds of up to 257km/h (160mph), according to the US National Weather Service (NWS). It warned the "very dangerous" storm could cause "catastrophic" damage, with "significant flooding from torrential rains" possible and waves potentially nearly 11m (35ft) high on Monday. The western Pacific region is particularly prone to tropical cyclones - though storms of this strength are unusual for the US islands.

The storm is forecast to bring winds in excess of 160mph and waves nearly 11m high when it makes landfall on Monday.

The island's civil defence office said at 13:00 local time (03:00 GMT) on Sunday that one of the evacuation sites had already reached maximum capacity and that people were being redirected to another site. Bavi is currently hurtling towards the US Pacific territories and is due to make landfall early on Monday Bavi has been classified as a super typhoon by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), a part of the US Navy responsible for monitoring tropical storms in the western Pacific. A super typhoon has winds in excess of 130 knots (150mph). JTWC predicts that Bavi will have winds of 150 knots (173mph) when it arrives over the islands, with gusts reaching as high as 180 knots (207mph). The NWS considers super typhoons to have the equivalent destructive potential as a category four or five hurricane.

Super Typhoon Bavi rapidly intensified in the western Pacific Ocean and is forecast to strike the U.S. Mariana Islands, including Guam, as a super typhoon by Monday. Devastating winds, torrential rain and powerful storm surge are all possible. Bavi first became a tropical storm late Wednesday, and by early Friday it strengthened into a typhoon, which is what hurricanes are called in the western Pacific Ocean north of the equator. The storm reached super typhoon strength later in the day. It is centered more than 300 miles east of Guam, moving west at 7 mph. Despite being so far away, outer bands of the super typhoon are already starting to hit the U.S. Mariana Islands. As the forecast map below shows, Super Typhoon Bavi is expected to continue its west-northwest track over the next several days.
